Heavy rain swept through tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in Gaza City on Saturday, leaving families wading through water around their shelters. The flooding is making daily life increasingly difficult for people in the camps, who are now facing a third winter there. "This is the first day of rain, and of course we are already flooded," said Olfat El-Magdoub, a displaced Palestinian sweeping water from her tent. She said that when it rained two weeks ago she spent four days sleeping on blankets on the floor because the bedding was soaked. Rafiq Ghattas, who lives in the Mina camp, home to around 1,700 families, said conditions deteriorated within an hour of the rain starting. Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Gaza since the conflict began on October 7, 2023. #Gaza #GazaCity #Flooding #DisplacedPalestinians #Palestine #Winter #MiddleEast #CGTNEurope

This year’s olive harvest has been the most violent in recent memory, with settler attacks on Palestinian farmers reaching a new high. But for Masafer Yatta, this is only the latest escalation in a decades-long campaign by the Israeli state to expel Palestinians from their land by any means necessary. Working in coordination with the army and police, nearby settlers wage a ceaseless battle against the Palestinians living in this area. Professor Ilan Pappé describes what has been happening to Masafer Yatta since the 1970’s as “incremental colonization, ethnic cleansing, and oppression,” and to be here is to see it firsthand. But the people of Masafer Yatta have earned a reputation for themselves for their resistance to state and settler terror. They simply refuse to leave, and the Israelis simply won’t stop trying to force them to. The Nakba never ended. We’re just watching its latest act.

Tens of thousands of displaced Palestinians are facing heavy rain which has caused flooding across  70,000 tents in Gaza. The first major winter storm hit on Friday night, with water soaking mattresses, blankets and clothes, leaving families wading through muddy water and forcing some to abandon their makeshift shelters. Gaza’s Civil Defence says it received more than 1,500 distress calls in just 10 hours. Water levels in some camps rose by up to 40 centimetres. Dozens of damaged walls and buildings have also collapsed, with people injured. Emergency teams say they are struggling to respond because of shortages of fuel and damaged equipment, including water pumps. The UN estimates around 950,000 displaced people are living in areas at risk of flooding. Aid agencies say Gaza urgently needs more tents, shelter materials and heating supplies as winter sets in. #politics #gaza #palestine
